transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-05
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Ethan O'Riley, Samira Patel, Jon Park (Redwood) — Arjun Patel, Priya Nambiar, Liam Torres, Nora Khalil, Diego Alvarez (Petra)

---
Summary (auto): Postmortem-style checkin after 2026-03-02 degraded responses on payment-reconciliation route. Focus on reproducibility, immediate mitigations, and telemetry gaps.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we wanted to go over the degradation on Tuesday, walk through what we think happened, and align on next steps. anyone on Petra want to start with what you saw from your side?
[00:18] Arjun Patel: yeah thanks Maya. we had a pretty bad spike of 5xxs and an increase in tail latency around 13:15 UTC. it coincided with a billing batch that usually hits 2k qps but that day we had a flash around 2.8k for a couple minutes. customers saw slow responses and some transactions retried and failed.
[00:42] Priya Nambiar: just to add, our observability showed token-level latency climbed from median 60ms to 420ms and error rate jumped to 6%. we also saw node-level OOM-ish signs, not full OOM but GC/eviction thrash on the in-memory cache.
[01:04] Liam Torres: nginx logs show a high number of connection retries and 504s outbound to the inference pool. we grabbed pcap for the window and i'll share it.
[01:18] Maya Chen: thanks liam. Ethan, quick recap from our side?
[01:24] Ethan O'Riley: yeah, on our side the serving runtime saw a KV-cache eviction storm for the payment-recon model shards. a couple of things aligned: high seq length for some requests, which invalidated prefix cache hits; autoscaler triggered scale-in/scale-out churn; and because requests were hitting cold KV pages we had heavier memory pressure which led to longer GC pauses on a few nodes. the result was higher per-token latency and a wave of token timeouts.
[01:58] Diego Alvarez: when you say "KV-cache eviction storm" do you mean the prefix cache across the model workers or something else?
[02:06] Ethan O'Riley: yes primarily the per-worker prefix/KV cache. we saw a pathological access pattern where several long-horizon prompts caused the working set to exceed the configured cache target, and the cache policy kicked into aggressive eviction which breaks locality and increases recompute.
[02:28] Nora Khalil: were there any changes to quantization or model variants pushed that day? security wants to rule out a bad deploy.
[02:36] Maya Chen: no deploys to the model repo or runtime that match the window — our deploy logs show nothing. there was a config change in the customer's autoscaler around 12:50 UTC that increased warmup thresholds, not a Redwood push.
[02:52] Priya Nambiar: correct, we rolled an autoscaler tweak before the batch was run hoping to smooth warm starts; hindsight, it moved the timing window.
[03:03] Arjun Patel: can you explain the warmup threshold interaction?
[03:08] Ethan O'Riley: sure. the autoscaler change increased cooldown so nodes stayed idle longer before being torn down, but it also allowed more rapid scale-up when load spikes happened. that, combined with long-seq requests that didn't hit the prefix cache, caused many workers to be populated with cold state roughly at the same time which amplified GC and memory pressure.
[03:36] Liam Torres: there's also an ingress burst from a partner endpoint we didn't attribute earlier; that pushed concurrency higher.
[03:44] Maya Chen: so multiple contributing factors: higher-than-expected QPS, long sequence prompts (working set larger), autoscaler tuning, and cache policy not robust to that access pattern.
[03:58] Priya Nambiar: yes. what puzzles us is why the fallback to the smaller model variant didn't kick in sooner — our app-level timeout policy is 2s and Redwood's fallback rule is 1.5s on that route.
[04:12] Jon Park: i can walk through that. the route policy logic had a miss: during the eviction storm the routing heartbeats experienced jitter and the controller delayed marking instance health as degraded, so the canary fallback policy did not trigger until the cluster reported >20% error rate which was later. we have a PR to make routing heartbeat thresholds adaptive to queue depth.
[04:38] Arjun Patel: ok that explains delayed fallback. how confident are you in the root cause hypothesis vs other possibilities like hardware flakiness?
[04:47] Ethan O'Riley: we looked at host metrics and there's no SMART or NIC errors. kernel logs clean. so it's behavioral: cache pressure + scale churn. hardware looks stable.
[04:57] Diego Alvarez: is there a quick mitigation we can apply now? we need something before next week's peak.
[05:02] Maya Chen: we've got a 2-step mitigation plan: 1) short-term: change the cache eviction sensitivity and lower the threshold that triggers immediate fallback to the smaller model variant. 2) medium-term: a scheduling change to stagger worker warmup and tune autoscaler cool-down to avoid synchronized cold starts.
[05:24] Priya Nambiar: can you quantify risk of the short-term change? will it increase token generation cost?
[05:30] Ethan O'Riley: slightly, because larger cache retention keeps more state in memory which reduces recompute and therefore usually reduces per-token cost; but if retention is too large it can increase memory pressure causing evictions elsewhere. the short-term tweak is conservative: increase target cache size by 10% with a guard rail to cap overall memory consumption per worker. we think cost impact will be neutral-to-small positive but improve tail latency.
[05:57] Liam Torres: what's the rollback if we see memory pressure spike?
[06:01] Jon Park: we have an automatic rollback policy: if node memory >85% for 5 continuous minutes in canary pool, rule reverts to previous cache target and routes traffic off canary. that's what we'll test in canary.
[06:15] Arjun Patel: good. about telemetry gaps — Priya mentioned we didn't have visibility into KV access patterns historically. can Redwood provide more granular telemetry?
[06:25] Maya Chen: yes. we propose adding per-route KV-hit/miss heatmaps and per-worker cache working-set histograms in the console. we'll share a proposal doc. that requires a small instrumentation change and a 2-week rollout.
[06:39] Priya Nambiar: two weeks is fine, but we need faster interim signals. can you supply a one-off diagnostic package we can run?
[06:45] Ethan O'Riley: we can deliver a synthetic probe tool that simulates long-seq access patterns against your canary pool and outputs hit/miss rates; we'd run it with you and upload the results. should be a day to run once we have access.
[06:58] Nora Khalil: on security, the pcap and logs contain PII; what's the recommended way to share?
[07:05] Samira Patel: please upload to the S3 bucket with encryption enabled and we will pull via a presigned URL. we'll also redact fields on our side. we will send a short checklist for log sanitization.
[07:18] Diego Alvarez: so timeline — when do you want to run the canary?
[07:22] Maya Chen: propose to start a canary tomorrow with the short-term cache sensitivity change and the lower fallback threshold. we'll monitor 24 hours and if stable, broaden. action items will capture dates.
[07:34] Arjun Patel: ok let's talk specifics then — who owns what for the canary?
[07:38] Maya Chen: Redwood: implement cache sensitivity flag change in canary pool (Ethan), implement adaptive routing heartbeat thresholds (Jon), provide synthetic probe (Ethan). Petra: run probe and share logs (Liam), confirm traffic shaping for the canary (Priya), security signoff on logs sharing (Nora). Samira will schedule runbook handover.
[07:57] Liam Torres: i'm concerned about the autoscaler change — are you advising we revert our previous change?
[08:02] Ethan O'Riley: not necessarily revert, just tune cooldown to ensure nodes don't enter synchronized warmups. we'll give recommended values and a small test matrix.
[08:12] Diego Alvarez: any surprises or non-obvious risks we should be aware of?
[08:16] Jon Park: a risk: if the partner endpoint bursts are frequent, the short-term fix won't fully prevent thrash. we need traffic-shaping or rate-limiting upstream as an additional control.
[08:28] Priya Nambiar: we can add an upstream throttle for that partner for the next two weeks. Diego will coordinate.
[08:34] Arjun Patel: ok. anything else on the mitigation before we move to runbook and next steps?
[08:40] Maya Chen: one more note — we found a config corner case where cache compaction ran less often for models with seq length variance above 0.6; fixing that compaction cadence is in our medium-term backlog and we'll prioritize it higher.
[09:00] Priya Nambiar: can you put that in the public backlog for transparency?
[09:04] Maya Chen: yes we'll add a note to the shared doc.
[09:09] Diego Alvarez: let's cover communication and SLAs — Petra wants a short incident timeline to include in an internal customer note.
[09:16] Samira Patel: we'll supply an incident timeline draft and a one-paragraph customer-facing summary. prefer to push to you for review before you send externally.
[09:24] Arjun Patel: thanks.
[09:26] Maya Chen: ok i'll recap quickly. Redwood will: share triage notes and logs link, run KV-cache synthetic stress test, implement canary changes (cache sensitivity + lower fallback threshold), and prepare runbook handover. Petra will: run probe, share ingress logs/pcap, add upstream throttle for partner, and confirm traffic shaping for canary.
[09:54] Ethan O'Riley: i'll also push the routing heartbeat adaptive thresholds as a patch to the canary controller.
[10:00] Nora Khalil: security will review the log sharing checklist and confirm by tomorrow.
[10:06] Samira Patel: i'll schedule the runbook handover for 2026-03-12 16:00 UTC and invite both teams.
[10:12] Priya Nambiar: sounds good.
[10:15] Maya Chen: great. any final questions?
[10:18] Diego Alvarez: just one — is there any historical precedent where cache policy caused system-wide degradation?
[10:23] Ethan O'Riley: it's uncommon but we've seen similar patterns at other customers when long-horizon prompts collide with autoscaler behavior; we've improved policies since then but this particular combination was missed.
[10:34] Arjun Patel: ok thanks all. look forward to the canary results.
[10:39] Maya Chen: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the logs link and action items in email. end call.
